title: Existence of a local morphism to an ordinary affine monoid spectrum
statement: Let P be a fine commutative monoid and T any space with a sheaf A of commutative monoids, using the unsharpened spectrum A(P) and local morphisms of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] and [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. For every monoid homomorphism phi : P -> Gamma(T,A), there exists a sheafed-space morphism f : T -> A(P) local on all stalks whose pullback of the canonical numerator p is phi(p) for every p. No uniqueness or naturality is asserted.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.1.8(i) and its proof, printed p.99, using 3.1.2--3.1.6, pp.98--99. This is the unsharpened assertion (i), not the sharp-stalk assertion (ii). No Stacks tag states this monoidal-space result.

proof.text: Fix $\varphi:P\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal A)$. In any commutative monoid, $x+y$ is a unit if and only if both $x,y$ are units: an inverse $z$ of $x+y$ makes $y+z$ an inverse of $x$ and $x+z$ an inverse of $y$. Thus $\mathfrak p_t=\{p\in P:\varphi(p)_t\notin\mathcal A_t^\times\}$ is a proper ideal with addition-closed complement, including the possibility $\mathfrak p_t=\varnothing$. For $a\in P$, let $V_a=\{t:\varphi(a)_t\in\mathcal A_t^\times\}$. If $t\in V_a$, represent an inverse germ by a section $v$ near $t$; the germ equality $\varphi(a)_t+v_t=0$ holds as an equality of sections on a smaller neighborhood, by the germ definition [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Hence $V_a$ is open. The map $f(t)=\mathfrak p_t$ satisfies $f^{-1}D(a)=V_a$ and is continuous because the $D(a)$ form a basis.

source.place: VIII 3.1.8(i), proof, p.99: the prime ideal defined from inverse images of stalk units; continuity spelled out from 3.1.3 and 3.1.6.

proof.text:
On $V_a$, the local inverse sections of Step 1 agree on overlaps: two inverses $v,w$ of a section $s$ satisfy $v=v+(s+w)=(v+s)+w=w$. The sheaf gluing axiom therefore gives a global inverse $v_a$ of $\varphi(a)|_{V_a}$, also when $V_a=\varnothing$. Define
$$\lambda_a:P[a^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal A(V_a),\qquad p-na\longmapsto\varphi(p)|_{V_a}+nv_a.$$
This is well-defined even though $\mathcal A(V_a)$ need not be integral: equality $p-na=p'-n'a$ in $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ gives $p+n'a=p'+na$ in the integral monoid $P$; apply $\varphi$ and add $(n+n')v_a$. The formula preserves addition and extends $\varphi$. It is the unique such homomorphism since the image of $-a$ must be $v_a$. For an inclusion $D(b)\subseteq D(a)$, the localization restriction $P[a^{-1}]\to P[b^{-1}]$ of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] fixes $P$. Its composite with $\lambda_b$ and the restriction of $\lambda_a$ to $V_b\subseteq V_a$ agree on $P$ and send $-a$ to the unique inverse of $\varphi(a)|_{V_b}$, so agree everywhere. Thus the $\lambda_a$ commute with all basic-open restrictions.

source.place: VIII 3.1.8(i), p.99, the straightforward sheaf construction, using the explicit localizations and sheaf of 3.1.2--3.1.3, p.98.

proof.text: The functor $\mathcal G(U)=\mathcal A(f^{-1}U)$ is a sheaf on $X=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P$: inverse images carry an open cover and its pairwise intersections to an open cover and its intersections, so matching families glue by the sheaf axiom for $\mathcal A$. By [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], $\widetilde P(D(a))=P[a^{-1}]$. Apply clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] with coefficient category the commutative monoids, source $\widetilde P$, target $\mathcal G$, and basis $\{D(a):a\in P\}$. Step 2 supplies exactly its restriction-compatible family. We obtain a unique sheaf homomorphism $\psi:\widetilde P\to f_*\mathcal A$ having components $\lambda_a$ on the basic opens.

source.place: VIII 3.1.8(i), proof, p.99: extension to the structure sheaf; the general basis-extension theorem is the cited existing node (Stacks 009O).

proof.text:
For a prime $\mathfrak p$, [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood] gives its smallest neighborhood $D(b)$ and $P[b^{-1}]=P-F$, where $F=P\setminus\mathfrak p$. A germ at $\mathfrak p$ is uniquely its restriction to this smallest neighborhood, so [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] identifies $\widetilde P_{\mathfrak p}=P-F$ and the germ of a canonical numerator with that numerator. For $t\in T$ use $\mathfrak p=f(t)$ and $F=P\setminus\mathfrak p$. The induced stalk map from Step 3 sends
$$p-c\longmapsto\varphi(p)_t-\varphi(c)_t\qquad(p\in P,\ c\in F),$$
where the minus sign means addition of the inverse unit. Indeed each $c\in F$ is inverted on $D(c)$ and Step 2 gives this formula there. By the last equivalence of [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood], the numerator $p$ is a unit in $P-F$ exactly when $p\in F$. Since $c$ is a unit in $P-F$, the same criterion holds for $p-c$. Its image is a unit exactly when $\varphi(p)_t$ is a unit, which by the definition of $f(t)$ is again $p\in F$. Consequently the stalk map is local. Steps 1--3 define a local morphism $G(\varphi)$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.8(i), proof, p.99: the uniquely defined local map from the monoid localization; stalks from 3.1.2--3.1.4, p.98.

proof.text: On D(1), which is the whole spectrum, the section map constructed above sends each numerator p to phi(p), because the image of 1 and its inverse are both 1. Thus its global numerator pullback is exactly phi. This establishes existence, without using uniqueness or the affine universal property.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_local_affine_hom (P : Type u) [CommMonoid P] (hP : FineFan.IsFine P)
    (T : SheafedSpace CommMonCat.{u}) (φ : P →* T.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)) :
    ∃ f : T ⟶ affine P, FineFan.IsLocalMorphism f ∧
      (SheafedSpace.Γ.map f.op).hom.comp (affineSection P) = φ
